rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternating night and day, the sun, and the moon’s changing course and phases let people measure days, months, and years and know when rights, worship, and transactions are due.
rows.anchor: ويتبين بذلك حلول الحقوق، وأوقات العبادات والمعاملات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are among the finest visible bodies, yet are created servants under God’s power; worship belongs to God alone, since associating partners with Him is not forgiven.
rows.anchor: أنهما مخلوقان عبدان من عبيده، تحت قهره وتسخيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people arrogantly refuse exclusive worship, the angels near God glorify Him night and day; Ibn Kathir connects this to the verse saying others were appointed who would not disbelieve.
rows.anchor: يسبحون له بالليل والنهار وهم لا يسأمون

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet forbade cursing night, day, sun, moon, and winds, since they may be sent as mercy to some people and punishment to others.
rows.anchor: عن جابر (1) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تسبوا الليل ولا النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A barren, plantless earth revives and produces varied crops and fruits after rain; its revival demonstrates God’s power to resurrect the dead and His power over all things.
rows.anchor: هامدة لا نبات فيها، بل هي ميتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the reward of believers, the passage contrasts the disbelievers’ painful punishment on the Day of Resurrection and judgment.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر المؤمنين وما لهم من الثواب الجزيل، ذكر الكافرين وما لهم عنده يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people received more provision than they needed, some would oppress others out of arrogance and ingratitude.
rows.anchor: لو أعطاهم فوق حاجتهم من الرزق، لحملهم ذلك على البغي والطغيان من بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah cites the maxim that the best livelihood is one that neither distracts a person nor makes him transgress.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: كان يقال: خير العيش ما لا يلهيك ولا يطغيك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah also recalls the Prophet’s fear of worldly splendor and the question whether good can bring evil.
rows.anchor: قتادة حديث: "إنما أخاف عليكم ما يخرج الله من زهرة الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chooses the amount of provision that benefits each person: He enriches whomever is suited to wealth and impoverishes whomever is suited to poverty.
rows.anchor: يرزقهم من الرزق ما يختاره مما فيه صلاحهم، وهو أعلم بذلك فيغني من يستحق الغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report cited in support says some servants are helped only by wealth, while others are helped only by poverty, and the opposite condition would corrupt their religion.
rows.anchor: إن من عبادي لمن (7) لا يصلحه إلا الغنى، ولو أفقرته لأفسدت عليه دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends rain after people have despaired of it, at the time they need it most; Ibn Kathir links this to the description of people’s despair before rain in 30:49.
rows.anchor: من بعد إياس الناس من نزول المطر، ينزله عليهم في وقت حاجتهم وفقرهم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spreads His mercy throughout the region and among its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: يعم بها الوجود على أهل ذلك القطر وتلك الناحية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah reports that during a drought, when a man told Umar that rain had failed and people despaired, Umar replied that they had been given rain and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: ذكر لنا أن رجلا قال لعمر بن الخطاب: يا أمير المؤمنين، قحط المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God directs creation toward what benefits them in this life and the next, and the outcome of all He decrees and does is praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: هو المتصرف لخلقه بما ينفعهم في دنياهم وأخراهم، وهو المحمود العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that when God commands the keepers of Hell to seize the condemned person, seventy thousand of them rush toward him.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى إذا قال للزبانية {خذوه} ابتدره سبعون ألفا منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned disbeliever is hauled away, dragged and shoved from behind.
rows.anchor: أي: سوقوه سحبا ودفعا في ظهره

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses the command as taking the person and pushing him.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: {خذوه فاعتلوه} أي: خذوه فادفعوه

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s line uses the cognate تعتل for being dragged back, illustrating the force of اعتلوه.
rows.anchor:
وقال الفرزدق:
ليس الكرام بناحليك أباهم … حتى ترد إلى عطية تعتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The center of Hell is meant by “the middle of the Blaze.”
rows.anchor: إلى سواء الجحيم} أي: وسطها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pouring of scalding water over the head recalls the description of boiling water poured over heads that melts what is in bellies and skin.
rows.anchor: يصهر به ما في بطونهم والجلود} [الحج: 19، 20]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Referring to an account cited earlier, Ibn Kathir says an angel strikes the victim with an iron mace, splitting his head, then boiling water runs through him and expels his intestines through his heels.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم أن الملك يضربه بمقمعة من حديد، تفتح (6) دماغه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address calling the condemned “mighty and noble” is spoken sarcastically to mock and rebuke him.
rows.anchor: قولوا له ذلك على وجه التهكم والتوبيخ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reports Ibn Abbas’s gloss: the condemned is neither mighty nor noble.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك عن ابن عباس: أي لست بعزيز ولا كريم

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrimah recounts that Abu Jahl boasted to the Prophet that neither the Prophet nor his Lord could overcome him and called himself mighty and noble; after God killed and humiliated him at Badr, this verse taunted him with his own words.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: لقي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أبا جهل -لعنه الله-

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites sit with the Prophet and hear him without understanding; after leaving, they ask the knowledgeable Companions what he said.
rows.anchor: حيث كانوا يجلسون إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ويستمعون كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آنفا means “just now” or “a moment ago.”
rows.anchor: قال آنفا} أي: الساعة، لا يعقلون ما يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s sealing leaves them without sound understanding or a sound intention, and they follow their desires.
rows.anchor: أي: فلا فهم صحيح، ولا قصد صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who seek guidance are enabled by God to find it, remain firm in it, and receive more of it.
rows.anchor: وفقهم الله لها فهداهم إليها، وثبتهم عليها وزادهم منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants them their God-consciousness by inspiring them with right judgment.
rows.anchor: أي: ألهمهم رشدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour’s signs are already here; the Prophet’s mission is one of them because he is the final messenger, through whom God completed the religion and established proof for humanity.
rows.anchor: فبعثة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أشراط الساعة؛ لأنه خاتم الرسل

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri says that Muhammad’s mission is one of the signs of the Hour; Ibn Kathir affirms his view.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: بعثة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم من أشراط الساعة. وهو كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s names include Prophet of Repentance, Prophet of Battle, the Gatherer who precedes the gathering, and the Last, after whom no prophet comes.
rows.anchor: أنه نبي التوبة، ونبي الملحمة، والحاشر الذي يحشر الناس على قدميه

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد
rows.claim: Sahl reports that the Prophet illustrated how close his mission is to the Hour by holding up his middle and index fingers together.
rows.anchor: حدثنا (3) سهل بن سعد قال: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال بأصبعيه هكذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity descends from one soul, Adam, and his spouse Eve, whom God made from him.
rows.anchor: خلقهم من نفس واحدة، وجعل منها زوجها، وهما آدم وحواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clans or peoples (shuʿūb) are broader than tribes (qabāʾil); further subdivisions include lineages, families, clans, and branches.
rows.anchor: وهي أعم من القبائل، وبعد القبائل مراتب أخر كالفصائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative view takes shuʿūb as subdivisions of non-Arabs and qabāʾil as subdivisions of Arabs, like the Israelite tribes.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالشعوب بطون العجم، وبالقبائل بطون العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people are equal in their earthly descent from Adam and Eve; they differ in religious merit through obeying God and following His Messenger.
rows.anchor: فجميع الناس في الشرف بالنسبة الطينية إلى آدم وحواء سواء، وإنما يتفاضلون بالأمور الدينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of peoples and tribes is that people recognize one another by lineage; the point follows the prohibitions on backbiting and looking down on others and underscores shared humanity.
rows.anchor: منبها على تساويهم في البشرية: {يا أيها الناس إنا خلقناكم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the phrase by identifying someone through a family name and tribe, as in saying whose son he is and where he belongs.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد في قوله: {لتعارفوا} ، كما يقال

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says the Himyar identified themselves by their regions, while the Arabs of the Hijaz identified themselves by their tribes.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري: كانت حمير ينتسبون إلى مخاليفها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet’s advice to learn enough genealogy to maintain kinship, which brings affection among relatives, increases wealth, and lengthens life; al-Tirmidhi calls the report gharīb and says it is known only by this route.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "تعلموا من أنسابكم ما تصلون به أرحامكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People’s standing with God depends on piety, not ancestry.
rows.anchor: إنما تتفاضلون عند الله بالتقوى لا بالأحساب

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet named the most God-fearing as most noble; when asked about Arab lineages, he said the best in pre-Islamic times are best in Islam if they gain understanding, and he also named Joseph’s noble prophetic ancestry.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أي الناس أكرم؟

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet said God looks at people’s hearts and deeds, not their appearance or wealth; Muslim and Ibn Majah transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة (7) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله لا ينظر إلى صوركم

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: The Prophet told Abu Dharr that no red or black person is better than him except through greater piety; Ahmad alone transmits this report.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له: "انظر، فإنك لست بخير من أحمر

rows.speaker: محمد بن حبيب بن خراش العصري
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Habib reports from his father that the Prophet said Muslims are brothers and no one has merit over another except through piety.
rows.anchor: سمعت محمد بن حبيب بن خراش العصري، يحدث عن أبيه: أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول (13) : المسلمون إخوة

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa reports the Prophet said all are children of Adam, who was created from dust, and warned people to stop boasting of their forefathers or become lower before God than dung beetles.
rows.anchor: عن حذيفة (4) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "كلكم بنو آدم.

rows.speaker: البزار
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar says the report from Hudhayfa is known only through this route.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: لا نعرفه عن حذيفة إلا من هذا الوجه

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that during the conquest of Mecca the Prophet preached from his camel, saying God had removed pre-Islamic pride in ancestry: people are either pious and honored by God or wicked and lowly; he recited this verse. Ibn Kathir notes Abd ibn Humayd also transmits it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: طاف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم فتح مكة على ناقته القصواء

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: Uqba ibn Amir reports that lineages are no ground for disparagement: all people descend from Adam, and only religion and piety confer merit; abusive, miserly, obscene behavior is blameworthy.
rows.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن أنسابكم هذه ليست بمسبة

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir’s wording of the report says all people descend from Adam and Eve, are alike as an unfilled small measure, and will be judged for piety rather than ancestry; Ibn Kathir says this route is absent from the six canonical collections.
rows.anchor: ولفظه: "الناس لآدم وحواء، طف الصاع لم يملئوه

rows.speaker: درة بنت أبي لهب
rows.claim: Durrah bint Abi Lahab reports that the Prophet named the best people as those who recite most, fear God, command right, forbid wrong, and maintain kinship.
rows.anchor: عن درة بنت أبي لهب قالت: قام رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو على المنبر

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet admired nothing in worldly life and no person except one possessing piety; Ahmad alone transmits this report.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: ما أعجب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شيء من الدنيا، ولا أعجبه أحد قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows people and their affairs; He guides, misguides, shows mercy, punishes, and grants preference by His wisdom and knowledge.
rows.anchor: عليم بكم، خبير بأموركم، فيهدي من يشاء، ويضل من يشاء، ويرحم من يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars infer from this verse and the cited reports that marriage compatibility is not a condition beyond religion; other scholars rely on different evidence discussed in legal works.
rows.anchor: من ذهب من العلماء إلى أن الكفاءة في النكاح لا تشترط، ولا يشترط سوى الدين

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Al-Tabarani reports that when a man from Banu Hashim claimed to be closest to the Prophet, Abd al-Rahman answered that another person was more entitled to him, while the claimant had kinship to him.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن أنه سمع رجلا من بني هاشم يقول: أنا أولى الناس برسول الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the human and knows all his affairs, including the good and evil that his soul whispers inwardly.
rows.anchor: يعلم ما توسوس به نفوس بني آدم من الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound report from the Prophet says God pardons what the Muslim community’s souls whisper, provided people neither say it nor act on it.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "إن الله (1) تجاوز لأمتي

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearer ones are God’s angels, not God indwelling a person; interpreting the phrase as mere knowledge avoids indwelling or union, but Ibn Kathir says the wording does not require that reading.
rows.anchor: يعني: ملائكته تعالى أقرب إلى الإنسان من حبل وريده (3) إليه.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir compares this to God being nearer to the dying person than those present, while unseen, which he explains as the nearness of the angels.
rows.anchor: ونحن أقرب إليه منكم ولكن لا تبصرون} [الواقعة: 85] ، يعني ملائكته

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also compares the wording to God’s statement that “We” sent down the Reminder: angels brought the Qur’an by God’s permission.
rows.anchor: فالملائكة نزلت بالذكر -وهو القرآن-بإذن الله، عز وجل

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enables angels to be nearer to a person than his jugular vein; a person receives an angelic prompting as well as a satanic one.
rows.anchor: الملائكة أقرب إلى الإنسان من حبل وريده إليه بإقدار (6) الله لهم على ذلك

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet also described Satan as moving through the son of Adam like blood.
rows.anchor: الشيطان يجري من ابن آدم مجرى الدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two receiving angels are the pair who record a person’s deeds, one stationed on the right and one on the left, watching.
rows.anchor: يعني: الملكين اللذين يكتبان عمل الإنسان. {عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and others identify the companion as the Satan assigned to the person.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة، وغيرهم: هو الشيطان الذي وكل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection, Satan disowns the disbeliever, saying he did not mislead him; the man was already far astray, receptive to falsehood and resistant to truth.
rows.anchor: أي: ما أضللته، {ولكن كان في ضلال بعيد} أي: بل كان هو في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial echoes Satan’s declaration that he only invited people and they chose to follow him, so they should blame themselves.
rows.anchor: في قوله: {وقال الشيطان لما قضي الأمر إن الله وعدكم وعد الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human blames his companion for turning him from the Reminder, while Satan says the person was already far from the path of truth; God ends their dispute, saying He warned them through messengers, scriptures, and proofs.
rows.anchor: فيقول الإنسي: يا رب، هذا أضلني عن الذكر بعد إذ جاءني. ويقول الشيطان

rows.speaker: الحاكم
rows.claim: Al-Hakim says the report under discussion has no basis as a hadith from Abu Hurayra, Saʿid, or al-Zuhri.
rows.anchor: قال الحاكم: لا أصل له من حديث أبي هريرة، ولا سعيد، ولا الزهري

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali describes the Frequented House as the heavenly sanctuary al-Durrah above the Kaʿba, whose sanctity matches the earthly House; seventy thousand angels pray there each day and never return. Ibn Kathir also cites variants identifying Ibn al-Kawwa as the questioner.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا قال لعلي: ما البيت المعمور؟ قال: بيت في السماء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says it is a house opposite the Throne, inhabited by angels, with seventy thousand praying there daily and never returning; Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Rabi ibn Anas, al-Suddi, and others say likewise.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: هو بيت حذاء العرش، تعمره الملائكة، يصلي فيه كل يوم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah relates the Prophet’s explanation that the Frequented House is a heavenly mosque aligned with the Kaʿba: if it fell, it would fall upon it, and seventy thousand angels enter daily and do not return.
rows.anchor: قتادة: ذكر لنا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يوما لأصحابه: "هل تدرون ما البيت المعمور؟

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak claims that a group of angels called al-Hinn, from Iblis’s tribe, inhabit it; Ibn Kathir leaves the matter to God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: وزعم الضحاك أنه يعمره طائفة من الملائكة يقال لهم: الحن (1) ، من قبيلة إبليس

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: A report from Umar, from the Prophet, says the sea rises three times each night seeking permission to break over people, but God restrains it. An expanded version describes an unnamed coastal guard seeing it approach the mountain tops; Ibn Kathir notes the narrator is unidentified.
rows.anchor: حدثنا عمر بن الخطاب عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "ليس من ليلة إلا والبحر يشرف فيها ثلاث مرات
